contributions.anchor: the p2 Summary Page line 1 'TOTAL CONTRIBUTIONS RECEIVED' Column A 'Total this Period' (12,572.62, typed), which is also the printed grand total at the foot of the p4 'Campaign Donations' ledger (12,572.62)
contributions.detail: 4 transcribed rows sum to 155.00 + 131.31 + 500.00 + 11,000.00 = 11,786.31, against a printed anchor of 12,572.62 — a DELTA of -786.31 (the filer's total EXCEEDS his own rows). TRACED, UNIQUELY, AND NOT NUDGED: the ledger prints its own SUBTOTAL of 786.31 on the line between row 3 and the loan row, and 155.00 + 131.31 + 500.00 = 786.31 exactly, so that subtotal is the sum of the three rows above it. The printed grand total is 786.31 + 786.31 + 11,000.00 = 12,572.62 — i.e. the filer's SUM range INCLUDED ITS OWN SUBTOTAL LINE, double-counting the three donor rows. The attribution is unique because 786.31 is simultaneously (a) the printed subtotal, (b) the exact sum of rows 1-3, and (c) the exact size of the delta; no other cell on the page carries that figure. This is a NEW SUB-CLASS of the §D5 spreadsheet sum defect: not a range that starts or ends one line off, but a range that swallows an intermediate subtotal. The filer's arithmetic is retained verbatim as a fact about the document. Column B 'Year-to-Date Total' (52,515.93, handwritten) is cycle-scoped and was never summed as an increment; the 12,572.62 anchor is the PER-PERIOD cell as the utah regime requires.

expenditures.anchor: the p2 Summary Page line 2 'TOTAL EXPENDITURES MADE' Column A 'Total this Period' (15,311.53, typed), which is also the printed grand total at the foot of the p3 'Campaign Expenses 2014 30 Days after Primary' ledger (15,311.53, crop-verified at 900 dpi)
expenditures.detail: 18 transcribed rows sum to 16,313.11, against a printed anchor of 15,311.53 — a DELTA of +1,001.58 (the rows EXCEED the filer's printed total). TRACED, UNIQUELY, AND NOT NUDGED. All 18 amounts were re-read at 700 dpi and every one confirmed, and the row count was independently confirmed by the text-band scan (20 bands = header + 18 rows + total), so no row is missing and none is misread. An EXHAUSTIVE search over all 262,143 non-empty subsets of the 18 row amounts found EXACTLY ONE that sums to 1,001.58: rows 1, 2, 4 and 5 (291.45 + 174.70 + 40.01 + 495.42). The printed total is therefore the sum of the other fourteen rows. Those four rows are marked out on the page: their amount cells carry a literal '$' glyph and their Address cells are pasted CREDIT-CARD STATEMENT DESCRIPTORS ('WINCO FOO ... 06/13', 'THE HOME DEPOT ... 06/16') rather than typed addresses — the signature of cells pasted in as TEXT, which a spreadsheet SUM skips silently. (Row 18 also shows a '$' and IS inside the total, so the glyph alone does not predict exclusion; the subset search, not the glyph, is what settles it.) This is a further SUB-CLASS of the §D5 spreadsheet sum defect. Per §C5 the delta is retained verbatim with the omitted rows named, and no figure was adjusted. CORRELATED-ERROR SCREEN: not run across filings, because doing so would require differencing this filer's other covers, which the regime forbids; the attribution here is already unique inside this one document. Column B 'Year-to-Date Total' (54,863.96, handwritten) is cycle-scoped and was never summed as an increment.
